last_reply:
The previous turn already read Parsec's team-registration code, so this time I'm reading the code behind the newest feature, the admin "SigmaDesk로 제어" button. That is Parsec's own Connect routine. I'll also try again to settle how its peer IDs are made.Server: store and show the attempts.Now the app reports each attempt. Parsec-style links that carry `host_secret=` pass the secret along, classified by the 27-character rule.Using the recorded attempt ID in the app's status line.Clean build. Testing the attempt recording and the admin control log on a temporary server, including the 27-character access-link rule and a forbidden attempt.All four tests pass. Refreshing the node package and the live server, then updating the mechanics sheet.I read Parsec's Connect code with Ghidra and used what it showed. Every SigmaDesk connection now gets an attempt ID in Parsec's format and is reported to the server, which keeps a new "최근 제어 기록" (who, which node, how, when) in the admin console and refuses connections from people without permission.

Share links now carry their secret. Like Parsec, a secret of exactly 27 letters/digits counts as an access link and anything else as a share secret.

The build and check pass, four new automated tests pass, a test against a temporary server worked, and the live Docker server and node installer are updated. Two things are still waiting on you: running the install on 10.10.1.92 from your RDP session, and trying a real screen connection once RustDesk is on both PCs.
